note: Typical figures for one trial at each phase. Every one of these varies enormously by disease — a dermatology Phase 3 and a pain Phase 3 differ by nearly fivefold in cost — so these are middles, not rules.

phases.name: Phase 1
phases.asks: Is it safe, and at what dose?
phases.who: Healthy volunteers, usually — people with the disease when the drug is too toxic to give anyone else

phases.name: Phase 2
phases.who: Patients who have the disease, in one or two forms of it

phases.name: Phase 3
phases.asks: Is it better than what we already have, and what does it do to a lot of people?
phases.who: Patients across many hospitals and often many countries
phases.sites: dozens to a few hundred sites

phase4.name: Phase 4
phase4.asks: What shows up once it is on the market?
phase4.detail: Runs after approval, in thousands of patients, and costs about as much as a Phase 3 — roughly $19.95M per study. It is where rare side effects finally become visible, because the earlier phases were never large enough to see them.

sources: Per-study costs: Sertkaya et al. for HHS/ASPE, 'Examination of Clinical Trial Costs and Barriers for Drug Development' — averages across therapeutic areas of $3.8M (Phase 1), $13.35M (Phase 2), $19.89M (Phase 3) and $19.95M (Phase 4). The spread by disease area is wide: Phase 3 runs from $11.5M in dermatology to $52.9M in pain and anaesthesia.
Participant counts, site counts and durations: FDA, 'Step 3: Clinical Research', and standard clinical-research references.
Cost per participant is derived here by dividing the per-study cost by the typical enrolment, not taken from a source.
